{{short description|French mathematician (born 1954)}}
[[File:Denis Serre.png|thumb|Denis Serre]]

'''Denis Serre''' (born 1 November 1954) is a French mathematician who works as a professor at the [[École normale supérieure de Lyon]], where he has chaired the mathematics department since 2012.<ref name="cv">[http://www.umpa.ens-lyon.fr/~serre/cv.html Curriculum vitae] (in French), retrieved 2015-01-18.</ref> His research concerns [[partial differential equation]]s, [[hydrodynamics]], and [[conservation law]]s.

==Education and career==
Serre was born in [[Nancy, France]];<ref name="cv"/> he is the nephew of mathematician [[Jean-Pierre Serre]].<ref>[http://www.umpa.ens-lyon.fr/~serre/effet.html L'effet de Serre] (in French), D. Serre, retrieved 2015-01-18.</ref> He obtained his [[agrégation]] in 1977, and his doctorat de troisième cycle in 1978, before finishing a [[doctorate|D.Sc.]] in 1982 from the [[University of Paris-Sud]] under the supervision of [[Roger Temam]].<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=31281}}</ref> He worked as a student teacher at the ENS de St-Cloud (a precursor institution to the ENS de Lyon) from 1974 to 1978, at the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] in Orsay from 1978 to 1983, and at the [[Jean Monnet University|University of St. Etienne]] from 1983 to 1987, before returning to the ENS de Lyon in 1987.<ref name="cv"/>

==Publications==
Serre is the author of several books, including
* ''Systems of Conservation Laws'' (2 vols., Cambridge University Press, 1999 & 2000).<ref>Review of original French-language publication by Philippe G. LeFloch (1999), {{MR|1459988}} and {{MR|1459989}}.</ref>
* ''Matrices: Theory and Applications'' (Springer, [[Graduate Texts in Mathematics]] 216, 2002; 2nd ed., 2010).<ref>Review of ''Matrices'' by R. J. Bumcrot (2003), {{MR|1923507}}.</ref>
* ''Multidimensional Hyperbolic Partial Differential Equations: First-Order Systems and Applications'' (with Sylvie Benzoni-Gavage, Oxford University Press, 2007). {{isbn|9780199211234}}  <ref>Review of ''Multidimensional Hyperbolic Partial Differential Equations'' by Kenneth H. Karlsen (2008), {{MR|2284507}}.</ref>

==Awards and honors==
From 1992 to 1997 Serre was a junior member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]].<ref name="cv"/> He became a knight of the [[Ordre des Palmes Académiques]] in 2012.<ref name="cv"/> In 2014, he was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to [[Hyperbolic partial differential equation#Hyperbolic system and conservation laws|hyperbolic conservation laws]] and mathematical exposition."<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |date=2018-08-25 }}, retrieved 2015-01-18.</ref> On November 7–9, 2014, a conference on conservation laws was held in honor of his 60th birthday.<ref>[http://perso.ecp.fr/~lafittep/60ansDS/ Conference announcement] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006202813/http://perso.ecp.fr/~lafittep/60ansDS/ |date=2014-10-06 }}, retrieved 2015-01-18.</ref> He received the [[Blaise Pascal]] Prize in 1990, the [[Institut Henri Poincaré]] Prize in 2000 and the [[Jacques-Louis Lions]] Prize of the Académie des Sciences in 2017.
